page: Amazon Web Services t3a.small is an entry-level burstable instance within the General Purpose family, operating on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 vCPUs via multithreading. Hardware cache includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is set to 2.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include dedicated local storage or GPU accelerators, and its baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Performance profiles reflect its burstable nature and low-density resource footprint. Synthetic benchmarks place processing throughput in the bottom tier relative to the wider cloud ecosystem, recording a PassMark CPU score of 1798.16 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 584.79. Memory bandwidth reaches 20.25 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 10.76 GB/sec for uncached writes. In application-oriented workloads, the instance achieves 1.17 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 1.65 GB/sec. Lightweight natural language processing on a 135M parameter model reaches 45.42 tokens per second for prompt processing and 21.33 tokens per second for text generation.

The primary operational tradeoff of the t3a.small centers on CPU credit governance and strictly constrained memory. Sustained high-intensity utilization depletes burst credits, resulting in throttling back to baseline performance levels. As a result, the instance is not designed for continuous computational workloads, data manipulation pipelines, or memory-heavy applications. It delivers high cost efficiency when utilized for low-traffic microservices, light monitoring daemons, simple build runners, code repositories, or staging and development environments with intermittent access patterns.
